newsitem.title: SPAIN: EU response to Helms Burton called "defensive".
newsitem.headline: EU response to Helms Burton called "defensive".

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes on Tuesday called the European Union ban on complying with Washington's anti-Cuba Helms-Burton law "defensive".
The EU made it illegal for Europeans to obey Helms-Burton in order to counteract any damage to European firms from the law and make it easier to retaliate, Matutes said.

"It's not an offensive law, it's a defensive law. It intends to, and I think it does reduce to a minimum the negative effects that European firms may suffer from the Helms-Burton law," Matutes told reporters at a news conference.
The Helms-Burton Act was passed earlier this year to a chorus of indignation from some of America's closest friends and largest trade partners.

Among other things, it allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreign companies or individuals deemed to have gained from investments in property confiscated in Cuba since Fidel Castro's communist revolution of 1959.

The EU law will prohibit European individuals or companies from complying with the act -- which has been suspended by U.S. President Bill Clinton until January -- and allow them to reclaim damages in EU courts.
"It offers European firms the opportunity to go before courts in any EU country to complain against American companies that have sued them," Matutes said.
"It provides the means to recoup the damages that the American companies inflicted by acting against their (European firms') properties in Europe," he added.

EU diplomats believe Clinton -- ahead in all polls to retain the U.S. presidency -- passed the act only because of Congressional pressure in an election year and is likely to further suspend it further in the new year.
Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Monday the EU decision was "an historic breakthrough which shows we have the will and capacity to defend our interests."
Brittan said he hoped that now "the EU has levelled the playing field", he would be able to negotiate an equitable solution to the trade row.
